highlights.title: Hydrodynamic Natal Kicks and Formation of Black Hole Binaries
highlights.reason: This study performs 3D SPH simulations to investigate the hydrodynamic Tug-boat mechanism and black hole natal kicks in core-collapse supernovae, providing critical physical limits on whether natal kicks can tilt binary orbits to produce negative effective inspiral spins $\chi_{\rm eff} < 0$.

highlights.title: Neutrino pair annihilation in curved spacetime: a fast moment method and the geometry of flavour conversion
highlights.reason: This work establishes an exact angular moment framework for neutrino pair annihilation around black hole accretion discs and uncovers a fundamental general relativistic sign-reversal effect on flavour conversion, directly relevant to compact object central engines and relativistic jet launching in GRBs.

highlights.title: Entanglement in Collective Neutrino Oscillations on a Quantum Computer
highlights.reason: This paper investigates whether multiparticle quantum entanglement breaks the standard mean-field Quantum Kinetic Equations (QKEs) in core-collapse supernova and merger environments, providing vital theoretical and computational boundaries for neutrino transport in compact object central engines.

highlights.title: Testing influence of tides on gravitational wave emission with SPH code PHANTOM
highlights.reason: This study demonstrates how Newtonian SPH simulations with Love-number rescaling can rapidly capture tidal excess in binary neutron star gravitational waveforms, offering a computationally efficient tool for multi-messenger transient early warnings.

highlights.title: Bicoherence States from QPO-Accretion Flow Coupling in Black Hole X-ray Binaries
highlights.reason: This work develops an analytical light-curve coupling model to explain the physical origin of bicoherence patterns and state transitions in black hole X-ray binaries, providing valuable nonlinear timing diagnostic tools for compact object high-energy observations.

highlights.title: Modeling of the X-ray Flux and Polarization Energy Spectra of Black Hole X-Ray Binaries with the KerrC Code
highlights.reason: This work develops the kerrC spectro-polarimetric ray-tracing framework to interpret IXPE and XL-Calibur observations of black hole X-ray binaries, providing critical methodology to constrain corona geometry and black hole spin in compact object systems.

highlights.title: Probing flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter interactions with the flavor composition of high-energy cosmic neutrinos
highlights.reason: This paper investigates the flavor composition of high-energy cosmic neutrinos from blazar TXS 0506+056 under flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter interactions, providing physical constraints testable by IceCube flavor measurements.

highlights.title: Quasi-spherical fallback in binary neutron-star mergers: fuel and obstacle for extended emission
highlights.reason: This paper investigates whether quasi-spherical fallback in binary neutron star mergers can power secondary relativistic jets for extended emission while simultaneously choking them, directly addressing central engines, relativistic jets, and breakout physics.

highlights.title: GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626: A Candidate of Hierarchical Triple Mergers
highlights.reason: The paper investigates the first observational candidate for a hierarchical triple black hole merger pair (GW230729_082317 and GW231118_005626) in LVK O4a, providing valuable empirical constraints on compact object mergers and dynamical assembly in dense environments.

highlights.title: Activity of the ejected galactic nuclei and cosmic rays
highlights.reason: The paper investigates UHECR acceleration in shocks driven by ultrafast outflows (UFOs) from ejected supermassive black holes, providing quantitative scaling relations for particle acceleration and photo-hadronic losses directly relevant to high-energy outflows and compact object environments.

highlights.title: XMM-Newton observations of the highest field polar AR UMa: An extreme case of soft-blobby accretion
highlights.reason: This work presents comprehensive XMM-Newton X-ray/UV and optical observations of AR UMa ($B \approx 230\,\mathrm{MG}$), providing critical observational constraints on extreme magnetic accretion, diamagnetic blob fragmentation, and soft X-ray excess in compact object systems.

highlights.title: A possible connection between the ridge and hypotenuse in the bispectrum of black hole X-ray binaries through quasi-periodic modulation
highlights.reason: The paper provides an analytical multiplicative modulation model for black hole X-ray binary bispectra, showing that phase-locking between a quasi-periodic modulator and underlying broadband noise explains the observed ridge-hypotenuse web patterns and opposite-sign biphases.

highlights.title: Forecasting Fundamental-Plane Tests of Intermediate-mass Black Holes in Radio-selected Dwarf Galaxies
highlights.reason: This work is relevant to compact object high-energy astrophysics and jet-accretion scaling relations, developing a rigorous forward-modeling framework to test intermediate-mass black holes in dwarf galaxies using the radio/X-ray Fundamental Plane.

highlights.title: Superorbital period evolution of Hercules X-1
highlights.reason: This paper presents multi-decadal X-ray timing observations of the accreting pulsar Hercules X-1, offering valuable observational constraints on compact object superorbital period evolution and neutron star precession.

entries.title: Constraining Dust Attenuation Curves in Star-Forming Galaxies at Cosmic Noon Using Multiple Emission Line Ratios
entries.abstract: Dust attenuation remains a dominant systematic uncertainty in measurements of an emission line, and therefore galaxies properties derived from the emission lines such as star formation rates. Corrections based only on the Balmer decrement require an assumed attenuation-curve slope, even though that slope varies among galaxies. We use JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy from JADES to constrain effective dust attenuation curves for 386 star-forming galaxies at $0.5\leq z\leq7$. For each galaxy, we combine H$α$, H$β$, and one additional hydrogen recombination line and solve for the normalization $τ_V$ and slope $n$ of a power-law attenuation curve, allowing the slope to vary from galaxy to galaxy. We found slopes and normalization span a broad range even for galaxies at similar redshifts. Additionally, our method using Paschen transitions provided substantially greater constraints the attenuation-curve slope than Balmer-only combinations. When comparing to SMC-like or Calzetti-like corrections we find our method produces more consistent star formation rates with less scatter. These improved dust corrections provide an avenue to better describe star formation rates in the epoch of peak star formation and the early universe.

entries.title: Entanglement in Collective Neutrino Oscillations on a Quantum Computer
entries.abstract: Simulations on a quantum computer have been propounded as a next-generation tool for studying neutrino flavour oscillations in dense environments like supernovae or neutron star mergers. However, quantum advantage hinges on the presence of quantum entanglement in the neutrino ensemble, and it has been argued that such entanglement becomes negligible in the limit of large neutrino number density. Here, we address this question by explicitly simulating the multiparticle dynamics of entangled neutrino ensembles with a varying number of particles, $N$, on both classical and quantum hardware, and comparing our results to those obtained with conventional ``mean-field'' methods based on Boltzmann-type kinetic equations. For simple toy systems, we demonstrate both analytically and numerically that, indeed, the predictions of full multiparticle simulations agree with those of mean-field methods in the large-$N$ limit. Along the way, we develop novel algorithms for the efficient simulation of entangled neutrino gases on both classical and quantum hardware. We then discuss physical situations in which an entangled neutrino system \emph{cannot} be described through mean-field dynamics alone and quantum entanglement therefore becomes phenomenologically relevant. We comment on the conditions under which these scenarios may be realized in supernova cores or neutron star mergers.

entries.title: Phentax: A JAX implementation of the IMRPhenomTHM waveform model
entries.abstract: The upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is expected to be sensitive to thousands of white dwarf (WD) binaries in our galaxy, extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) of stellar-mass compact objects into massive black holes, stellar-mass black hole binaries (SOBHBs) in their early inspiral phase, and, crucially, massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) with masses in the range of $10^4$-$10^7 M_\odot$. The presence of such a large number of signals requires joint inference of all parameters across all sources present in the data, an approach referred to as "global fit". This requires evaluating hundreds of thousands of waveform templates, which can be computationally expensive. To address this challenge, we present $\texttt{Phentax}$, a $\texttt{JAX}$ re-implementation of the $\texttt{IMRPhenomTHM}$ waveform model. This is a state-of-the-art time-domain phenomenological waveform model for comparable-mass binary black holes that includes the effects of higher-order modes. Given this, $\texttt{IMRPhenomTHM}$ is one of the models currently used to simulate and analyze MBHB signals in LISA. With $\texttt{Phentax}$, we provide a fast, easy-to-batch, and differentiable implementation of this waveform model to accelerate the development of LISA global fit algorithms.

entries.title: FORGE'd In The Early Universe II: Constraining The Pop III Initial Mass Function
entries.abstract: We present a cosmological radiation-magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) zoom-in simulation of $56$ Population III stars using FORGE'd in FIRE. Our simulation combines a cosmological initial condition centered on an isolated ultra-faint galaxy ($M_{\mathrm{halo}} \sim 10^9 M_\odot$ at $z=0$) with individual-star formation and feedback physics, reaching a maximum mass resolution of $\sim 10^{-2} M_\odot$ and spatial resolution of $\sim 10^{-3} \mathrm{pc}$. We follow continued star formation for just over $500$ Myr, from $z \sim 16$ to $z \sim 7$, substantially longer than what has been achieved before, and track star formation across five distinct minihalos. From our stellar population, we self-consistently resolve an emergent stellar initial mass function (IMF) and find $α= 1.9$ for $dN/dM \propto M^{-α}$ at $M_{\star} \gtrsim 2.2 M_{\odot}$. Additionally, we form both single and multiple stellar systems, including binaries and higher-order multiples, as well as stars with masses below $1 M_{\odot}$. At early times, the stellar mass distribution is more top-heavy, with a high-mass slope of $α\sim1.4-1.5$, similar to previous Pop. III simulations, and steepens as star formation continues. This suggests that differences between our final IMF and previous studies may partly reflect the much longer evolution followed here, approximately five orders of magnitude longer than in several previous Pop. III sink-particle simulations. The first star-forming minihalo, which hosts the most massive stars in our simulation, has a shallower IMF slope of $α\approx 1$, while later-forming minihalos produce lower maximum stellar masses in lower-density parent clouds.

entries.title: Magnetically Arrested Accretion and Black Hole Spin in a Semi-Analytic Model of Galaxy Formation
entries.abstract: We present {\sc Mad Sage}, a semi-analytic model of galaxy formation that couples black hole mass and spin evolution to gas accretion and AGN feedback under magnetically arrested disk conditions. Building on the {\sc Dark Sage} model, we incorporate GRMHD-calibrated prescriptions for spin evolution and jet power, spin-dependent radiative efficiencies, and remnant spins from BH-BH mergers. We compare accretion and feedback models, including coherent disk-fed accretion with mixed coherent and incoherent hot-halo accretion, with and without additional mechanical feedback. We find that incoherent accretion, together with Blandford-Znajek spin-down, drives massive BHs toward low spins, reducing jet efficiencies and weakening the quenching of massive galaxies. Reproducing the high-mass end of the stellar mass function requires either exclusively coherent accretion or an additional feedback component provided by ADAF outflows. Our models broadly reproduce observed BH-galaxy scaling relations, disk surface density profiles, and the AGN luminosity function at $z\sim 2-6$, although the spin models under-predict the number density of faint AGN at low redshift. At $z\lesssim 3$, predicted BH spins decrease with increasing BH mass, while at higher redshifts, the mass dependence weakens. Spin distributions peak at $|a_\star|\sim 0.5$-$0.7$, below current X-ray reflection spectroscopy measurements, and become bimodal for massive, quiescent BHs accessible with the next generation Event Horizon Telescope and the Black Hole EXplorer. We report that the predicted LISA event rates are nearly independent of the adopted accretion and spin models.

entries.title: FORGE'd in Fragments: Pop III star formation in a Milky Way-like progenitor halo
entries.abstract: We present a radiation-magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) cosmological zoom-in simulation of Pop III star formation, drawing initial conditions from a Milky Way-like progenitor halo at redshift $z \sim 21$. We follow the collapse of primordial gas over 10 orders of magnitude, through to the formation of an accretion disk that becomes gravitationally unstable $Δt \sim -3$ kyr before the first protostar's formation. Prominent spiral arms then develop and fragment vigorously, producing $\sim 60$ sink formation events over the first $8$ kyr post-collapse evolution, with a total stellar mass reaching $> 150\,{\rm M_\odot}$ by $15$ kyr, the end of our simulation. The disk remains magnetically supercritical throughout: the mass-to-flux ratio falls from $μ_Φ\sim 10^2$-$10^3$ to $\sim 15$ by $15$ kyr, as the inflow brings in magnetic flux. The magnetic energy in the disk remains sub-dominant throughout, but grows by $\sim 3.5$ orders of magnitude after the first star forms. The disk starts sub-virial and reaches virial equilibrium within $\sim 2$ kyr. The total stellar mass of the population grows as $M_* \propto t^2$, confirming the prediction of accelerating accretion in self-gravitating turbulent collapse, at rates of $\dot{M} \sim 10^{-3}$-$10^{-2}\,{\rm M}_\odot {\rm yr}^{-1}$. The star formation efficiency reaches $\approx 90\%$ within the disk (after $\approx 11$ kyr; $\approx 80\%$ at $9.5$ kyr) and $\sim 50\%$ within a $0.1$ pc sphere. We find a top heavy IMF ($dN/dm \propto m^{-α}$) with a high-mass slope $α\approx 1$. The cosmological environment sets the boundary conditions of the disk: an envelope delivers $\sim 3\times 10^{-3}\,{\rm M}_\odot {\rm yr}^{-1}$ to the outer edge of a disk with a radius of $\sim 10^{3}$ AU; the disk spreads and, in our simulation, its fragmentation sites move outward, from $\sim 500$ to $\sim 1350$\,AU, until it has been depleted.

entries.title: Hydrodynamic Natal Kicks and Formation of Black Hole Binaries
entries.abstract: The observation of over 300 Gravitational Wave (GW) events by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration, has yielded information of the merger of compact object binaries, such as their individual masses and spins. However, the effective spin parameter obtained from the GW signal provides important information that could be used to discern the binary's formation channel. Overall, binaries formed from dynamic interactions in dense stellar environments are expected to have a random distribution of effective spins between -1 and 1. Meanwhile, binaries formed from the evolution of isolated stellar binaries are expected to have positive effective spins unless there is a large enough natal kick during the compact object formation that could significantly alter the orientation of the individual spins with respect to the binary's angular momentum. We study the viability of obtaining large natal kicks during the formation of massive Black Holes by studying the asymmetric mild explosion of $13\text{M}_{\odot}$, $21\text{M}_{\odot}$, $28\text{M}_{\odot}$ and $34\text{M}_{\odot}$ pre-supernova stellar models, by means of 3D Smooth Particle Hydrodynamics simulations. Our results show that, even kicks in the order of $\sim$ 1000 km/s, which are among the highest values observed for natal kicks, can't consistently change the orientation of the orbit. Physical setups where the orientation of the orbit changes require the kick to be directed correctly, and they would also require for the supernova explosion energy to be quite high.

entries.title: Jeans Dynamical Constraints on the IMF in Massive Quiescent Galaxies at $z\sim0.7$ from JWST/NIRSpec
entries.abstract: We present dynamical masses for nine massive quiescent galaxies at $z\sim0.7$ from the JWST-IMFERNO program, measured from ultra-deep ($\sim32$hr), spatially resolved NIRSpec/MSA spectroscopy combined with NIRCam imaging. The most massive of these galaxies have previously been found to have a bottom-heavy initial mass function (IMF), based on measurements of dwarf-sensitive absorption features. Here, we examine whether the stellar masses inferred for these IMFs are consistent with the dynamical masses of these galaxies. We derive the dynamical masses by including Jeans Anisotropic Modelling within a forward-modelling framework that accounts for instrumental optics, source morphology, and geometric effects. We compare the resulting dynamical masses to the stellar masses for different IMF assumptions. A Milky Way IMF produces physically plausible dynamical-to-stellar mass ratios but implies central dark matter fractions ($f_{\rm DM,1R_e}=0.54\pm0.06$) that are a factor $\sim2$ higher compared to local ETGs and simulations. When uniformly applying the IMF that was measured from absorption features, the mean dark matter fraction becomes low ($f_{\rm DM,1R_e}=0.02\pm0.18$), and the stellar masses exceed the dynamical mass at $2σ$ significance for two out of seven galaxies in the sample. When we adopt the measured IMF only in the central $R_e$ and use a MW IMF in the outskirts, we find realistic dark matter fractions ($f_{\rm DM,1R_e}=0.28\pm0.12$) and consistent dynamical masses. These results support a scenario where the cores of the most massive quiescent galaxies at $z\sim0.7$ had a bottom-heavy IMF, similar to those observed in the centres of local early-type galaxies. Our results are consistent with an inside-out growth scenario, in which size and mass growth of massive galaxies proceeds after quenching through minor mergers, leaving the bottom-heavy cores mostly intact.

entries.title: Digging into the Interior of Hot Cores with ALMA (DIHCA). VIII. Feeding a high-mass binary system in the making
entries.abstract: We analyze the gas kinematics in the proto-binary NGC 6334I(N) ALMAe9-ALMAe14 system with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 1.33 mm with an angular resolution of 66 mas (~90 au). With a separation of 740 au between the system members, these observations allow a detailed study of the gas motion around this likely binary system hosting at least one growing high-mass star. Some CH$_3$OH lines tracing cold gas ($E_u/k_B$~100 K) reveal the presence of ordered circumbinary gas motion around the binary system within a ~1000 au radius, and rotation around the individual sources with rotation axes pointing roughly in the same direction. We estimate a central source mass, uncorrected for inclination, of 2 M$_\odot$ for the secondary, while the primary has an estimated mass of 5 M$_\odot$ as reported in previous works. The CH$_3$OH transitions with higher $E_u/k_B$ ($\gtrsim400$ K) values reveal circumstellar gas rotation in ALMAe9 consistent with the cold gas tracers. The vibrationally excited SO emission also traces rotation around ALMAe9 and potentially an accretion shock from a flow feeding the circumstellar disk of ALMAe14. We identify two potential inflows feeding the circumstellar disks from the circumbinary gas at rates of ~$10^{-6}-10^{-4}$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ from CH$_3$OH emission. An additional third inflow seems to be feeding the primary from gas at larger scales.

entries.title: Testing influence of tides on gravitational wave emission with SPH code PHANTOM
entries.abstract: In this article, we demonstrate how a Newtonian SPH (Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics) code PHANTOM can be used to estimate the tidal contribution to gravitational wave (GW) waveforms. Using a binary neutron star (NS+NS) system with typical masses of 1.5 + 1.5 Msun as an example, we show - by comparing our results with waveforms calibrated against full numerical General Relativity (GR) simulations - that the tidal contribution to GWs can be reliably extracted using as few as about 10$^4$ smoothed particles. Naturally, one must account for the difference in neutron star compactness between Newtonian gravity and general relativity. At separations greater than 100 km, the relative tidal contribution falls below the level of numerical noise inherent in SPH; however, at such distances, GW waveforms for point-like sources are sufficient for detection purposes. For a white dwarf-neutron star (WD+NS) binary with typical masses of 0.6 Msun and 1.5 Msun respectively, a much larger number of smoothed particles is required, along with a separation on the order of tens of thousands of kilometers, as tidal mass transfer and the disruption of the white dwarf begin quite rapidly. Nevertheless, these challenges can be overcome, but the approach is not capable of yielding useful results due to the richness of Newtonian effects. In all cases, it is crucial to perform a hydrostatic/hydrodynamic relaxation (HPR) of the initial models; otherwise, the entire GW signal is lost in the numerical noise.

entries.title: TRGB Distances to the Andromeda Dwarf Satellites from the INT Monitoring Survey
entries.abstract: We measure tip of the red giant branch (TRGB) distances to 17 dwarf satellites of M31 from Sloan $i$-band photometry of the Isaac Newton Telescope (INT) monitoring survey of Local Group dwarf galaxies, and add the distances of And I, And VII and And IX from earlier papers of the survey. We locate the tip with a Sobel edge-detection filter applied to the luminosity function of stars within two half-light radii of each galaxy. The distance moduli range from $23.38 \pm 0.06$ mag (And XVI, 474 kpc) to $25.35 \pm 0.06$ mag (And XVIII, 1177 kpc), and 15 of the 20 satellites lie between 650 and 850 kpc. For most galaxies, our distance agrees with at least one published value. Compared with Conn et al. (2012), our tip is brighter for 12 of the 18 galaxies in common, by up to 0.39 mag, possibly because of crowding in the central regions. And XII lies at $844^{+40}_{-38}$ kpc, about 60 kpc behind M31, consistent with a first infall into the Local Group. And XXII lies at $753^{+28}_{-27}$ kpc, closer than all earlier estimates, and about 59 kpc from M33 in three dimensions (for an M33 distance of 794 kpc), consistent with an association with M33. And XVIII lies about 400 kpc behind M31, too far for a secure association with M31.

entries.title: Expanding the Volatile Abundance Inventory for High-Priority K-Dwarf JWST Exoplanet Systems
entries.abstract: There are exceedingly few chemical abundance measurements available in the literature for K dwarf stars, especially for those with T$_{eff} <$ 4700 K due to an incompatibility of traditional analyses with their molecular-line-ridden optical spectra. To address the need for K dwarf abundance constraints, we present an elemental ([C/H], [O/H]) and isotopic ($^{12}$C/$^{13}$C, $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O) abundance analysis for six K dwarf exoplanet host stars: K2-141, NGTS-10, WASP-43, WASP-69, WASP-80, and HATS-72. Each system hosts an exoplanet targeted by JWST characterization efforts, making host star abundances especially critical as baseline references. Using MARCS model atmospheres, the TurboSpectrum spectral synthesis code, and near-infrared IGRINS spectra, we derive novel [C/H] and [O/H] abundance ratios for these high-priority K dwarf host stars. We further investigate prospects for determining $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C and $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O ratios using $^{13}$C$^{16}$O and $^{12}$C$^{18}$O lines from the 2.3 micron CO bandhead. The observed spectra are too noisy to measure $^{16}$O/$^{18}$O ratios for the sample, but we do find sub-solar $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratios for five out of six targets. We also derive uniform gyrochronological ages for each host star to compare with galactic chemical evolution models and identify underlying abundance-age trends. NIR H+K band spectroscopy provides an alternative to optical, atomic line-derived carbon and oxygen abundances for cool dwarf stars. The growing catalog of precise host star elemental and isotopic abundances complements ongoing observations of their companions and provides a baseline for understanding their chemical composition, origin, and evolution.

entries.title: Coherent radio emission at 45 MHz from the nearby planet-hosting star GJ 725A
entries.abstract: Ultra-low-frequency (<100 MHz) coherent radio emission from exoplanet-hosting stellar systems carries information about planetary and stellar magnetic fields, as well as the space weather environment - information that is difficult to obtain at other wavelengths. We carried out the circularly polarized LOFAR LBA Sky Survey, the most sensitive circularly polarized survey in this frequency range, using the LOFAR low-band antenna system. As part of this untargeted search, we detected a signal in a 1h observation that is coincident with the quiescent, planet-hosting, solar-neighborhood M dwarf GJ 725A at a distance of 3.5 pc. The signal has a high circular polarization fraction of $74\pm16$% and a peak brightness of $B=135\pm17$ mJy/beam between 42 MHz and 50 MHz. It was undetected in the 50-66 MHz range, with a 3$σ$ upper limit of $B<48$ mJy/beam, corresponding to a drop of at least a factor 3 across 12 MHz, and indicating a strong spectral feature or cutoff around 50 MHz. Our detection represents the lowest-frequency confirmed detection of a stellar system. Based on the high estimated brightness temperature ($\sim10^{14}$ K), transient character and polarization fraction, the emission is most plausibly attributed to the electron cyclotron maser instability. The available observations are not sufficient to identify the astrophysical origin of the emission. We consider three plausible scenarios: auroral emission of a yet undetected wide-orbit giant planet with a magnetic field $B\geq18$ G, star-planet interaction with the known 11 d orbit terrestrial planet GJ 725Ab, or an origin due to stellar magnetic activity. Ultra-low-frequency monitoring, combined with new, preferably simultaneous observations in the X-rays, UV, and H$α$, and a search for a wide-orbit (thousands of days) giant planet across the full allowed parameter space will allow us to distinguish between these scenarios.

entries.title: Constraining the Merger Fraction and the Upper Mass Limit of Ultramassive White Dwarfs
entries.abstract: We performed a spectroscopic survey of all known white dwarfs with $M \geq 1.3~M_\odot$ and $T_{\rm eff}\geq11,000$ K identified through Gaia DR3 astrometry from the Gentile-Fusillo et al. (2021) catalog. Of the 293 white dwarf candidates that met our criteria, 259 had no optical spectroscopy or spectral classification available in the literature. We obtained follow-up spectroscopy on 97% of this sample and performed a detailed model atmosphere analysis to constrain the atmospheric composition and mass for each object. For a selection of magnetic white dwarfs, we use offset dipole models to constrain the magnetic field strength and geometry and calculate the magnetic fraction as a function of mass. We use magnetism, unusual atmospheric composition, kinematics, and rapid rotation rates to identify merger remnants, and constrain the merger fraction to be $53_{-6}^{+7}$% for white dwarfs more massive than $1.3~M_\odot$. Hence, roughly half of the most massive white dwarfs likely form through binary mergers. We also use our sample to derive an empirical upper mass limit for white dwarfs in the solar neighborhood. Including the General Relativistic effects, the most massive white dwarf in our sample, J0318+7923, has $M=1.33-1.35~M_\odot$ depending on the unknown core composition. Furthermore, because our temperature criteria overlap with the ZZ Ceti instability strip, we find a new selection of ultramassive pulsator candidates that may provide an excellent opportunity to probe the interiors of crystallized CO or ONe-core white dwarfs.

entries.title: Neutrino pair annihilation in curved spacetime: a fast moment method and the geometry of flavour conversion
entries.abstract: Neutrino-antineutrino annihilation above black-hole accretion discs is shaped both by general-relativistic transport and by neutrino flavour conversion. Whether these effects can be treated independently depends on how gravity weights the different flavour populations. We investigate this interplay using backward ray tracing in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, combined with an exact angular-moment formulation of the annihilation kernel that we validate against the analytic spherical solution and published disc calculations. We first establish that flavour-conversion corrections are independent of the spacetime geometry when conversion is uniform and the initial heavy-lepton neutrino emission is negligible. For uniform conversion, this separability remains approximately valid when the flavour-dependent emitting regions overlap: compared with the same discs in flat space, moving with the same local velocities, gravity enhances the deposited energy by factors of 1.4-5, while changing the relative conversion effect by no more than 6% for most temperature profiles considered; conversion that varies across the disc raises this to 22% around a rapidly spinning hole. A qualitatively different regime emerges when heavy-lepton neutrinos originate from an inner ring separated from the electron-flavour emitting regions. Relativistic bending and energy shifts preferentially enhance annihilations involving inner-ring neutrinos, producing relativistic conversion factors up to 2.4 times the flat-space ones. In one configuration, flavour equipartition reduces the deposition by 54% in flat space but increases it by 11% in Kerr spacetime. These results identify the spatial arrangement of flavour-dependent neutrinospheres as a key determinant, in the models considered, of whether flavour conversion and relativistic transport can be treated separately.

entries.title: The Complex Magnetic Anatomy of a White Dwarf Chromosphere
entries.abstract: This study presents phase-resolved spectroscopy and spectropolarimetry of the DAHe white dwarf LP 705-64. Here, two apparently discrete chromospheric regions are observed to alternate in visibility and magnetic polarity with rotation, with field strengths of 9.5 and 22 MG based on the measured Zeeman splitting in Hα. As in the class prototype GD 356, emission line equivalent widths vary in antiphase with the broadband light curve. The 9.5 MG field is visible for 60 per cent of the stellar rotation and stays nearly constant, whereas the 22 MG field increases modestly during the remaining phases. Notably, the time-series transitions between magnetic regions are abrupt and transit-like in morphology, requiring at least one magnetic region to be highly localised and significantly smaller than the areas inferred for the dark surface spots. Both the intensity and the Stokes V/I spectra indicate a field configuration significantly more complex than an offset dipole, but higher-cadence data are necessary to distinguish between a global field and localised magnetic regions. All data are consistent with magnetic, chromospheric, and dark surface regions that are co-located and thus physically related. These findings support a model of chromospheric emission that is intrinsic and localised, consistent with predictions of dynamo-driven electrical currents that heat the upper atmosphere near magnetic poles.

entries.title: Bicoherence States from QPO-Accretion Flow Coupling in Black Hole X-ray Binaries
entries.abstract: We calculate the bispectrum of a black hole X-ray binary light curve model where lognormal fluctuations associated with the inner flow are multiplicatively modulated by a quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) and its harmonic. The bispectrum is a third-order Fourier statistic which measures the strength of nonlinear relationships between frequencies in a timeseries. When applied to black hole X-ray binaries, the bispectrum reveals nonlinear coupling between QPOs and the broadband noise. These couplings are sorted into a small set of states and X-ray binaries are observed to transition between these states as they undergo spectral transitions. We show that the model we consider is able to reproduce all of the canonical bispectral states analytically. We consider other sources of incoherent variability which dilute this model light curve and find that changes in this dilution, together with changes in the QPO amplitude, drive the transitions between the bispectral states. We also show that the larger QPO amplitudes of high-inclination sources favor the cross state and the weaker QPOs of low-inclination sources favor the hypotenuse state, which can explain the empirically observed correlation. Additionally, any dilution by equatorial winds, which are seen mainly at high inclination, would push high-inclination sources further toward the cross state.

entries.title: Interferometric survey of stellar parameters. Reliable methodology for a direct measurement of the angular diameter in exoplanet host stars
entries.abstract: Since their pioneer observations more than thirty years ago, exoplanets have been a major topic among the astrophysics community. Despite their ubiquity, our knowledge of planetary parameters and internal compositions still mostly relies on stellar quantities estimated through evolutionary models, which suffer from a calibration bias, preventing the community to have accurate discussions on the diversity of planets across the Universe. We use our sample to demonstrate the current best reachable precision of the CHARA Array to be $\sim$ 2% on radius determination, with an error budget dominated by the uncertainty on the angular diameter, while systematics are shown to be of the order of 1% thanks to our methodology. While the precision matches values found in the literature, we demonstrate the uniqueness of the present study in the relevance of the results put forward. Finally, we show that our methods naturally translate into an improved accuracy of the planetary parameters, along with an improvement in precision by $\sim$ 50% in radius and $\sim$ 30% in mass.

entries.title: KCWI Observations of Type 2 Quasar-driven Ionized Outflows at z~0.1
entries.abstract: AGN-driven outflows play a crucial role in regulating star formation in galaxies. These outflows are known to be multi-phase, and the characterization of the kinematics, extent, and energetics of each gas phase is needed to obtain a full picture of the outflow properties and impact. This study presents Keck Cosmic Web Imager (KCWI) integral field spectroscopy of the ionized gas outflow properties in seven low redshift (z<0.1) quasars---six Type 2 AGN and one narrow-line Type 1 AGN---providing insight into the warm ionized outflows in these luminous AGN. With the large field-of-view and high sensitivity of KCWI, these data reveal both larger ionized outflow extents than were previously known for these sources and uncover the existence of additional high-velocity kinematic components in the ionized outflows of these luminous AGN. We find (a) a high incidence (50-70%) of multiple outflows on scales of 4--10 kpc and (b) trends between the outflow extent, kinematics, and the ionized mass and energy outflow rates. These trends imply that the faster and often smaller outflows carry higher mass and energy outflow rates than the slower, larger outflows. We also find that the ionized gas outflows reach as far as the known extent of narrow-line ionized gas emission in AGN, which is known to depend weakly on AGN luminosity. This work highlights the utility of the current generation of wide-field integral field spectrographs on 8--10m class telescopes for studying quasar-driven outflows.

entries.title: Unlocking Pandora's Secrets: Probing the Thermodynamics of Abell 2744
entries.abstract: Abell 2744 (Pandora's Cluster) is a massive galaxy cluster undergoing multiple mergers, characterized by a highly disturbed X-ray morphology, elevated intracluster medium (ICM) temperatures, and several radio relics associated with merger driven shocks. We present NuSTAR observations of Abell 2744 aimed at mapping its thermodynamic structure and constraining the presence of inverse Compton (IC) scattering from relativistic electrons. We measure the temperature distribution across the cluster and identify a prominent shock front with a Mach number of $\mathcal{M} = 1.58^{+0.42}_{-0.30}$, aligning with the southeastern boundary of the radio halo. The global NuSTAR spectra are modeled with single- and two-temperature thermal components, as well as thermal plus power-law models to test for IC emission. The spectra are well described by purely thermal models with an average temperature of $kT \approx 11$ keV, and we find no significant evidence for non-thermal hard X-ray emission. We derive a 90\% confidence upper limit on the $20-80$ keV IC flux of $ F_{\rm nt} < 2.31 \times 10^{-12} erg~s^{-1}~cm^{-2}$. Combining this with 1.5 GHz diffuse radio measurements from the VLA, we estimate a lower limit on the average magnetic field strength of $B > 0.2 \ \rm{μG}$.

entries.title: A pipeline for identifying astrophysical signals and instrumental glitches in LISA data
entries.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is a space-based gravitational wave detector scheduled for launch in the 2030s by the European Space Agency. Operating in the 0.1 mHz to 0.1 Hz band, LISA will observe a variety of astrophysical sources including but not limited to supermassive black hole mergers, extreme mass ratio inspirals, and white dwarf binaries. LISA will yield new insights, including supermassive black hole formation, new tests of general relativity, population studies of white dwarfs and others. Like all interferometric gravitational wave detectors, LISA data is expected to contain non-astrophysical transients, commonly referred to as glitches. We introduce a two step pipeline that consists of a search algorithm for detecting potential transients in simulated LISA data followed by a machine learning model that classifies the detected transients as gravitational waves or instrumental glitches. This is important for MBHBs with very high masses (around $10^6\ M_{\odot}$) which are transients that could be morphologically similar to LISA glitches in the data. Initial results demonstrate a promising ability to classify detected events with an accuracy close to $98\%$. The pipeline also shows the ability to analyze a month of data in under 2 minutes on a laptop. This shows an eventual utility of our pipeline for enabling accurate rapid alerts from low latency searches. It could also support model selection in global-fit analyses by providing an initial summary of the location and type of individual signals. This paper also discusses challenges encountered during training, including limitations of the current framework.

entries.title: Modeling of the X-ray Flux and Polarization Energy Spectra of Black Hole X-Ray Binaries with the KerrC Code
entries.abstract: In this chapter, we introduce the kerrC model, an advanced framework designed for the analysis of combined spectral and polarimetric X-ray emission from black hole systems. The model is built upon an extensive dataset of ray-tracing Monte Carlo simulations that compute the radiative transfer of X-rays in the strongly curved spacetime near the event horizon of a Kerr black hole. These simulations incorporate thermal seed emission from a geometrically thin, optically thick accretion disk, along with the subsequent Comptonization processes within a hot corona of variable geometry and physical properties. Crucially, the reflection of both primary disk and Comptonized photons is treated self-consistently utilizing the xillver reflection tables, and the polarization 4-vectors of the photons are rigorously transported throughout the simulation to preserve full polarization information. The code tracks photons forward in time, allowing for multiple photon scatterings in the corona and off the accretion disk. We detail the underlying mechanics of the ray-tracing simulations and the fitting models, and discuss the applications of kerrC in leveraging X-ray polarization observations to constrain black hole spin and coronal geometry.

entries.title: Predicting Continuum Emission in Massive Star-Forming Regions with Embedded HII Regions - Dust, Free-Free, and Anomalous Microwave Emission with POLARIS
entries.abstract: Context: HII regions are a key stage of massive star formation, where ionizing radiation reshapes the interstellar medium. Their continuum spectra trace thermal dust, free-free emission, and anomalous microwave emission (AME). Aims: We investigate how these components evolve as an HII region expands and correlate with gas and electron column densities across spatial scales. Methods: We post-process RAMSES radiation-magnetohydrodynamical simulations of a $10^4 M_\odot$ cloud with POLARIS. The model includes grain charging, rotational excitation and damping, radiative torques, rotational disruption, and emission from dust, ionized gas, and nano-composite grains. We compute maps and SEDs for six snapshots over $1-10^4$ GHz and analyze multi-scale correlations. Results: Ionized emission evolves from a compact, optically thick HII region to an extended, optically thin structure. Around 15 GHz, free-free emission changes from a $ν^2$ to a $ν^{-0.1}$ spectral regime as optical depth decreases, and increasingly traces electron column density. The thermal dust peak shifts from mid- to far-infrared as colder material contributes, while dust emission remains strongly correlated with total gas column density. AME peaks at 26-37 GHz and shows scale-dependent correlations with gas and electron distributions. Rotational disruption is the main dust-destruction mechanism affecting mid-infrared emission and the high-frequency AME tail. Conclusions: These continuum components provide complementary, scale-dependent diagnostics of stellar feedback. Self-consistent multi-frequency modeling is essential for interpreting surveys of star-forming clouds.

entries.title: Tidal Braking Does Not Dominate Open-Cluster Slow Rotators
entries.abstract: Extended main-sequence turn-offs (eMSTOs) observed in open clusters younger than $2~\mathrm{Gyr}$ are commonly attributed to a spread in stellar rotation rates. Tidal synchronization in close binary systems has been proposed as a possible mechanism for producing slowly rotating stars. To test this hypothesis, we measured the radial-velocity (RV) dispersions of slow-rotator samples associated with the eMSTOs of eight open clusters using ESO VLT/GIRAFFE and SALT/RSS spectroscopy. We extended the analysis to 40 open clusters using Gaia DR3 RV measurements. The observed cluster RV dispersions are generally substantially smaller than those predicted for binary populations dominated by close systems with orbital periods for which tidal synchronization is expected to be effective. In particular, all 40 clusters in the Gaia sample have RV dispersions below the prediction of the $P=10$ d binary-population model. These results suggest that close, tidally synchronized binaries are unlikely to be the dominant origin of slow-rotator populations in young and intermediate-age open clusters, although a contribution from undetected or wider binary systems cannot be excluded.

entries.title: Identifying Chemically Coherent Stellar Families in the Galactic High-α Disk with Low-Resolution Spectroscopy
entries.abstract: Identification of chemical substructures in the Galactic high-α disk provides valuable insight into its formation history. In this work, we demonstrate the capability of low-resolution spectroscopy for this purpose by applying DBSCAN clustering to 87,275 red giants in the high-α disk using 18 elemental abundances derived from LAMOST low-resolution spectra (R~1800). We assess the effectiveness of this approach by comparing the clustering results from the low-resolution data with those obtained by applying the same procedure to high-resolution survey abundances and to mock catalogs. These comparisons suggest that, despite the relatively large uncertainties in individual elemental abundances derived from low-resolution spectra, the astrophysical coherence among different elements provides sufficient information to identify chemically coherent families that may share similar enrichment histories without necessarily sharing a common birth environment. After scanning the parameter space of the DBSCAN procedure and merging the results from different parameter combinations, we identify 133 candidate chemical families containing 4,642 unique stars (5.3% of the high-α disk sample). These families exhibit diverse multi-element abundance patterns, with particularly prominent differences in neutron-capture elements at nearly identical [Fe/H] values. These families therefore offer new constraints on the diversity of chemical enrichment pathways and on the assembly history of the high-α disk.

entries.title: Baryon Number Susceptibilities of Hot and Dense Nuclear Matter in Relativistic Mean-Field Models
entries.abstract: We develop a fully analytical framework for calculating baryon number susceptibilities in relativistic mean-field (RMF) models of hot and dense nuclear matter at finite temperature and baryon chemical potential. The formalism is applied to representative nonlinear RMF parameterization sets to investigate the model dependence of baryon number fluctuations over a wide range of temperatures and baryon chemical potentials. All the considered RMF parameterizations reproduce the overall qualitative beam-energy dependence of the cumulant ratios. The observed skewness and kurtosis within the RMF models satisfy the experimental values. Specifically, the FSU-family parameterizations exhibit relatively small deviations from the measured heavy-ion observables i.e. cumulant ratios.

entries.title: Probing flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter interactions with the flavor composition of high-energy cosmic neutrinos
entries.abstract: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos probe non-standard neutrino interactions over cosmological distances. We study flavor-dependent interactions between neutrinos and dark matter (DM) for neutrinos produced inside the dense DM spike surrounding the supermassive black hole of the blazar TXS~0506+056. A flavor-diagonal potential $V_α=A_α\,ρ_χ(r)$ induced by coherent forward scattering modifies the mixing in the medium, and the flavor-dependent scattering cross section attenuates the neutrino flux along the line of sight. We show that the propagation is adiabatic throughout the spike and the halo, so that the matter eigenstates produced at the source are conserved and only re-projected onto flavors at Earth. Two regimes emerge. For $A\ll 10^{-38}\,{\rm cm^3}$ the mixing is unaffected and the IceCube three-flavor composition limits the cross section to $σ_{νχ}/m_χ\lesssim 10^{-28}\,{\rm cm^2/GeV}$. For larger $A$ the interacting flavor is isolated into a single matter eigenstate at the source; the two remaining eigenstates escape without attenuation, producing a survival plateau that relaxes the limits by up to four orders of magnitude. The sign of the potential can differ between neutrinos and antineutrinos, so that the isolated state connects to different vacuum mass eigenstates for $ν$ and $\barν$, which leaves a characteristic imprint on the flavor composition even without attenuation. The requirement that the potential induced by the dark matter density around Earth do not affect the observed PMNS matrix, so that the flavor projection at Earth is performed with the local matter mixing, gives A$\lesssim 10^{-30}\text{cm} ^3$. The combined constraints are presented in the $(A,σ_{νχ}/m_χ)$ plane and compared with a vector-mediator benchmark.

entries.title: Dynamical formation of Gaia neutron star binaries in star clusters as a phase-dependent process
entries.abstract: Gaia has discovered dormant compact-object binaries in which the compact object shows no observable interaction with its luminous companion. These systems, hereafter Gaia BHs and Gaia NSs for black hole (BH) and neutron star (NS) companions, provide a new probe of compact-object binary formation. These detached systems are difficult to produce through standard isolated binary evolution alone, and their formation pathways remain unclear. Previous $N$-body studies have shown that Gaia BH-like objects are formed efficiently in star clusters, while Gaia NS-like objects are not. This has been attributed to the BH subsystem dominating the cluster core. We performed direct $N$-body simulations of $10^4 \mathrm{M}_\odot$ star clusters in a Galactic tidal field and investigated how NS-main-sequence (NS-MS) binaries form during the late BH-depleted phase. We found that NS-MS binaries satisfying Gaia-sensitive criteria form only after BH depletion. NSs are present in the core throughout the evolution, but the strong encounters there are monopolized by the BH subsystem until it is depleted. Our results show that the dynamical formation of Gaia-sensitive NS-MS systems is not prevented in star clusters, but delayed relative to Gaia BH-like systems.

entries.title: Phosphorus-rich star formation in giant molecular clouds hosting primordial globular clusters
entries.abstract: Recent observational studies have identified phosphorus-rich (P-rich) stars ([P/Fe]>1.0) in both Galactic globular clusters (GCs) including three confirmed cases and the field population. Using analytical models of GC formation, we investigate a scenario in which P-rich stars form from pristine gas in GC-forming giant molecular clouds (GMCs) polluted by oxygen-neon (ONe) novae within and surrounding the GMCs. Within this framework, we model the chemical abundance patterns of P-rich stars using diverse chemical yield sets for ONe novae while varying the dilution factor (Fdil), defined as the ratio of pristine gas mass to total ONe nova ejecta mass. The principal results of our models are as follows: Across a wide range of Fdil, most models display positive correlations between [P/Fe], [N/Fe], [O/Fe], [Al/Fe]$, [Si/Fe], [S/Fe], and [Si/S]. The [Ce/Fe] ratios in P-rich stars can reach values up to 1 if the GMCs are additionally polluted by interacting low-mass asymptotic giant branch stars.P-rich star formation is highly unlikely in environments with a low interaction frequency between GMCs and ONe novae. P-rich stars exhibit anomalously low 14N/15N, 16O/17O, and 16O/18O isotopic ratios, offering a clear observational diagnostic to test this scenario. Assuming that P-rich Galactic field stars originate from GCs, we discuss the origin of their chemical abundance patterns. We suggest that the existence of P-rich stars provides direct evidence that GC-forming GMCs were polluted by pre-existing stellar populations.

entries.title: SEDust: A DUSTY-Based SED-Fitting Pipeline for Dust and Mass-Loss from AGB and LPV Stars
entries.abstract: We present SEDust, an automated pipeline for spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting and the estimation of stellar mass-loss and dust-production rates. We apply this pipeline to quantify the mass-loss and dust injection rates in the dwarf galaxy NGC~6822, focusing on long-period variables (LPVs) and pulsating asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars as major contributors to dust feedback into the interstellar medium. The total stellar mass-loss rate is found to be $(3.70 \pm 1.16) \times 10^{-3}\ M_{\odot} \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. Two alternative methods (an LPV-based estimate and DESK) give totals that differ from this value by factors of $\sim$2.3 (lower) and $\sim$2.4 (higher), respectively, which we adopt as an estimate of the method-dependent systematic uncertainty. A positive correlation between stellar luminosity, intrinsic reddening caused by circumstellar dust self-extinction, and mass-loss rate is observed. The specific mass-return rate from AGB stars is $(7.40 \pm 2.30) \times 10^{-11}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, indicating that mass return from AGB stars alone is insufficient to sustain the current star formation rate of NGC~6822. This result implies the need for external gas accretion or additional mass-return mechanisms.

entries.title: Probing Dark Matter via the Migdal Effect in LUX-ZEPLIN Data
entries.abstract: Sub-GeV dark matter (DM) particles deposit little energy in conventional direct-detection experiments and are therefore difficult to probe, but the Migdal effect provides an electronic signal from atomic ionization accompanying the recoil. Using the new results of the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment with a 4.2 tonne-year exposure, we evaluate the sensitivity of the Migdal effect to the spin-independent DM--nucleon scattering cross section. For masses between $350~\mathrm{MeV}$ and $10~\mathrm{GeV}$, the projected 90\% upper limits range from $6.5\times10^{-37}$ to $9.6\times10^{-42}~\mathrm{cm^2}$. These limits are then used to constrain the minimal scalar- and vector-mediator DM models. For the light-mediator DM model, the constraint on the coupling reaches $α\simeq 10^{-12}$, which is stronger than or comparable to the constraints from kaon decays, stellar cooling, and SN1987A.

entries.title: Chromospherically Active Stars in the MeerKAT Galactic Plane Survey
entries.abstract: Stellar magnetic activity has long been established to occur in subsets of late-type main-sequence stars and manifests itself in the form of chromospheric and coronal activity. This activity is driven by magnetic fields generated by dynamo mechanisms associated with stellar rotation and convection, which channel and dissipate magnetic energy to the outer atmospheric layers. Optical spectroscopic follow-up was carried out for 99 radio-X-ray coronally active stars of G-, K-, and M-spectral types in the SARAO MeerKAT Galactic plane survey point sources. There are 46 stars that exhibited chromospheric activity. Specifically, 39 stars show Ca II H&K emission lines, whereas 18 show Ca II IRT, 11 show both H&K and IRT lines. Of the 39 stars displaying H&K emission, 37 show activity levels greater than the Solar minimum activity. Their X-ray to bolometric luminosity ratios are within the coronal thresholds of > -4.5. In addition, we explored optical photometry to investigate the rotation information and found that these stars show short rotation periods; in comparison with activity levels, the activity levels dampen as the rotation periods increase. We also analysed optical light curves for a subset of stars, and they show flaring behaviour at the same epoch as enhanced chromospheric activity, indicating the flares and chromospheric emission are manifestations of the same underlying magnetic activity process.

entries.title: Quasi-spherical fallback in binary neutron-star mergers: fuel and obstacle for extended emission
entries.abstract: Extended emission (EE) lasting hundreds of seconds has been observed in a fraction of short gamma-ray bursts (sGRB) containing both nonthermal and thermal components, and representing a significant puzzle for models involving binary neutron stars (BNSs). Recent GRMHD simulations of BNS mergers found that the late-time fallback is approximately quasi-spherical and motivated an r-process powered thermal model for EE. However, the available radioactive-heating power may be insufficient to sustain the luminosity inferred by such a model. We therefore propose a fallback-fed secondary-jet scenario in which a fraction of the fallback material circularizes on the black-hole equatorial plane and powers the jet, while polar fallback impedes its propagation. Using a semi-analytic toy model, we follow the propagation of the jet-head through the fallback envelope and identify jet-dominated, cocoon-dominated, and choked scenarios. The boundaries of these regimes depend primarily on the circularization fraction $f_{\rm circ}$, on the jet half-opening angle $θ_j$, and on the polar refilling factor $ξ_{\rm pol}$, with the approximate scaling $\widetilde{L}\propto f_{\rm circ}/(ξ_{\rm pol}θ_j^2)$. By post-processing data from BNS-merger simulations we find that the fraction of bound fallback material that avoids prompt capture is $f_{\rm npc}\simeq0.52$, thus providing an upper bound on the circularizable fallback supply. Under suitable prescriptions for nonthermal jet emission and thermal emission from the jet head, the estimated isotropic-equivalent $0.3$--$10$ keV energies reproduce well both the observed EE distribution for the jet-dominated branch and its low-energy end for the cocoon-dominated branch. Overall, these results suggest that fallback-fed secondary jets represent a dynamically feasible and energetically consistent explanation of the EE in sGRBs.

entries.title: Suppression of water-ice UV photodesorption on cosmic dust analogs
entries.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) photodesorption regulates the partitioning of water between interstellar ice mantles and the gas phase, yet laboratory yields are generally measured on planar substrates rather than on surfaces representative of cosmic dust. We investigate how grain morphology affects UV photodesorption from thin H$_2$O ice films of 2-6 monolayers deposited on planar gold and olivine, soot nanoparticles, and olivine microparticles. Samples were irradiated at 12 and 60 K with a microwave-discharge hydrogen lamp, and ice depletion was monitored by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and reflection-absorption infrared spectroscopy. On planar gold, the photodesorption yield increases approximately linearly with ice coverage, from $\sim5\times10^{-4}$ to $\sim2\times10^{-3}$ molecule photon$^{-1}$ between 2 and 6 monolayers, consistent with increasing UV absorption in optically thin ice; planar olivine gives comparable yields. In contrast, photodesorption is suppressed on particulate olivine and, more strongly, on soot, where yields are up to a factor of $\sim40$ lower than on gold at 12 K. Both experimental techniques confirm the strong suppression of ice depletion on soot. These results show that UV photodesorption depends not only on ice coverage but also strongly on grain morphology. The pronounced suppression on soot may reflect heterogeneous ice growth and altered energy redistribution within nanoscale ice domains, implying that yields measured on planar substrates may substantially overestimate photodesorption from the thin ice mantles of cosmic dust.

entries.title: The N/O-O/H relation across large-scale environments
entries.abstract: The large-scale structure (LSS) of the Universe shapes galaxy evolution through its intricate web-like morphology, yet its specific influence on gas-phase chemical abundances remains uncertain. Particularly, a homogeneous comparison of the N/O$-$O/H relation, a tracer of the mass assembly and baryonic cycle, across distinct LSS environments has been lacking. In this study, we analyse a local SDSS galaxy sample curated within the framework of the CAVITY project -- dedicated to studying void galaxies -- in which galaxies are classified by their LSS environment into three groups: clusters, voids, and non-cluster/non-void (NCNV). We extract spectroscopic emission line fluxes from the central SDSS spectra and analyse how different galaxy properties affect the scatter in the N/O$-$O/H relation. For that, we subtract the main N/O$-$O/H relation from the data and study the dependence of the resulting residuals ($ξ_\text{N/O}$) on a set of parameters, including stellar mass ($M_\star$), $g-r$ colour, and star formation rate (SFR). We find that $M_\star-$related variables are the best predictors of the scatter in the N/O$-$O/H relation, with little influence of the recent star formation history. Regarding the LSS comparison, no significant differences are found for void and NCNV galaxies. Cluster galaxies, however, present a N/O$-$O/H relation systematically lower (with $ξ_\text{N/O} \sim -0.02$). Consistent with this shift and with $M_\star$ as a good predictor of N/O$-$O/H deviations, we find that environmental dependences are also reflected in fundamental scaling relations: both the MZR and N/O$-M_\star$ relations are different for cluster galaxies. These combined results point to mechanisms in the dense intracluster medium (such as strangulation or re-accretion of metal-enriched gas) as the primary drivers of these chemical offsets for galaxies in cluster environments.

entries.title: Successive Decimetric Bursts Associated with Breakout Magnetic Reconnection during the Decay Phase of an M-Class Flare
entries.abstract: Radio imaging spectroscopy diagnoses coronal electron acceleration and propagation by tracking energetic electron beams and locating energy-release sites. Using MUSER (0.4-2 GHz) and SDO data, we investigate decimetric radio emission during an eruption with an M1.1 flare on 17 December 2014. The eruption involves a twisted coronal structure evolving through three stages: a violent internal eruption, a rise-and-expansion phase, and a breakout eruption. The flare peaks at 01:50 UT during the internal eruption, while the cluster of successive type III-like decimetric bursts occurs in the decay phase, linked to the breakout eruption. The radio source coincides with a high-squashing-factor Q region from nonlinear force-free field (NLFFF) extrapolations, indicating a quasi-separatrix layer (QSL). We interpret the radio emission as consistent with plasma emission driven by nonthermal electrons accelerated by breakout reconnection at this QSL, between the outer envelope of the erupting structure and the surrounding corona. The successive bursts occur in the decay phase because breakout reconnection involves a larger, more energetic twisted structure at higher altitude, where an extended high-Q region, favorable acceleration geometry, and repeated sub-eruptions sustain efficient electron acceleration. Missing soft X-ray enhancement suggests most accelerated electrons escape upward or lose energy before reaching the chromosphere. The concentrated source positions of the successive radio bursts suggest pseudostreamers may act as particle accelerators, trapping electrons and directing them along a narrow layer. These results establish decimetric radio imaging as a powerful diagnostic of breakout reconnection and particle acceleration in the solar corona, with implications for energy release in pseudostreamer environments.

entries.title: GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626: A Candidate of Hierarchical Triple Mergers
entries.abstract: Hierarchical triple mergers denote a sequential merger process in which the black hole remnant from an initial binary merger subsequently merges with a third black hole. In this study, we identify a related pair of binary black hole mergers, GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626, which exhibit consistent sky localization and luminosity distances; the latter is identified as a candidate hierarchical merger binary back holes. The Bayes factor in favor of a hierarchical triple merger origin over the non-association hypothesis is $110$. However, after accounting for the priors odds, the corresponding odds ratio decreases to $0.1$, indicating that the current evidence is insufficient to favor the hierarchical triple merger scenario. GW230720\_0823 show no detectable signatures of orbit eccentricity or line-of-sight acceleration. The inferred properties of these two gravitational wave events suggest a dynamical formation channel, such as few-body scattering or gas-assisted mergers, while a primordial triple origin is disfavored. Among the proposed dynamical environments, the accretion disk of an active galactic nucleus provides the most plausible site. We further derive constraints on the local rate of hierarchical triple mergers rate under both the null and candidate scenarios. Under the assumption of no detected hierarchical triple mergers, the most stringent $90\%$ confidence upper limit is $4.2\,{\rm Gpc^{-3}yr^{-1}}$ for $t_{\rm max}=10$ years using the GWTC-4 catalog.

entries.title: Activity of the ejected galactic nuclei and cosmic rays
entries.abstract: The double and triple approaches of supermassive central black holes are a fairly common process in the hierarchical picture of galaxy formation. In this case, the ejection of a black hole is possible; it may carry the accretion disk and some amount of stars with it. The activity of the galactic nucleus can be restored after the ejection. One consequence of this activity is an ultrafast gas outflow, accompanied by a shock wave. We show that the acceleration of cosmic rays at such a shock is more effective than in the case of a stationary galactic nucleus due to the lower density of the surrounding gas and the higher velocity of the shock front. In this case, proton acceleration can occur up to energies of ~10^{19} eV, which is an order of magnitude higher than in an ordinary nucleus in the centers of galaxies.

entries.title: Existence of Distinct Strong and Weak Shear Regimes of Self-Generated Turbulent Magnetic Reconnection
entries.abstract: Magnetic reconnection can become fast in three-dimensional turbulent layers. However, the parameters and mechanisms that control the fast state are not yet fully clear. Existing guide-field simulations of self-generated turbulent reconnection show locally coherent flux-rope structures embedded in a stochastic layer, motivating a flux-rope-mediated picture, with reconnection rates of order $V_{\rm rec}/V_A \sim 0.01$ in MHD. Here, we test whether and how magnetic shear changes the reconnection regime, using 3D resistive-MHD simulations at $S_L=10^5$. We vary the guide field while keeping the initial reconnecting field strength and rate normalization fixed, comparing a guide-field, weaker-shear configuration with the anti-parallel, strong-shear limit. We find that the strong-shear regime is qualitatively distinct from the flux-rope-mediated guide-field regime. Rather than retaining a narrow layer and locally coherent flux-rope structures, the current layer develops short-wavelength corrugations that broaden it substantially, and the reconnection layer electric field is sustained by fluctuation EMF. The reconnection rate increases to $V_{\rm rec}/V_A \sim 0.03$, about three times the guide-field value. These results indicate that magnetic shear can select the mechanism controlling fast 3D turbulent reconnection, shifting the system from a guide-field regime consistent with flux-rope mediation toward a very fast turbulence-broadened regime. This transition provides a novel explanation for the sudden switch-on of fast reconnection in eruptive solar flares.

entries.title: The OpenMULTI3D stellar analysis package. A 3D non-LTE spectrum synthesis code for AFGKM-type stars within the DISPATCH framework
entries.abstract: Upcoming large spectroscopic surveys such as WEAVE, 4MOST, and SDSS-V will provide millions of high-resolution stellar spectra. This motivates the development of efficient codes to perform three-dimensional (3D) non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (non-LTE) radiative transfer (RT) calculations, in order to meet the requirements on efficiency and data analysis quality set by these surveys. We present a new open access 3D non-LTE spectrum synthesis code OpenMULTI3D, based on its predecessor MULTI3D, which was never released. This code can be used to compute large grids of spectra of AFGKM-type stars and will aid the exploitation of large-scale spectroscopic surveys such as 4MOST. We summarise the main input micro- and macro-physics of the code, describe its numerical implementation and provide selected test cases. The outputs of the code are compared with standard results in the literature, including the NLTE departure coefficients in 1D and 3D, the 3D NLTE abundance corrections, 3D synthetic spectral energy distributions for three types of stars, and 3D NLTE Balmer-line profiles of a metal-poor red giant. We also demonstrate how the code can be used to compute time-dependent spectra of stars, which may be relevant in precision stellar physics and analyses of exoplanet spectra. OpenMULTI3D offers an accessible and efficient platform for high-fidelity stellar analysis in the era of large-scale spectroscopic surveys.

entries.title: Where the red rise stops: JWST/MIRI reveals a near-infrared turnover in the Little Red Dot Abell2744-QSO1
entries.abstract: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are compact sources with a blue rest-frame UV, a steep red optical continuum and, often, broad hydrogen lines. They have been interpreted as dense stellar systems, dust-reddened active galactic nuclei, or black holes embedded in dense, dust-poor gas, scenarios that are hard to tell apart in the rest-frame UV and optical. We present JWST/MIRI F770W and F1000W imaging of the triply lensed Abell2744-QSO1 at z=7.04, probing rest-frame 0.96 and 1.24um. QSO1 is unresolved, and its steep optical rise stops near rest-frame 1um. Up to 1.24um, a T~4450K blackbody, or a hotter one reddened by dust, describes the continuum, with no sign of the hot dust seen in most type-1 quasars. Our statistically preferred SED fits produce the red continuum with (3-4)x10^9 Msun of stars, over 100 times the dynamical limit on the host mass, and are therefore disfavoured. An accretion disc in a dense gas cocoon respects this limit but over-predicts the 1.24um flux by 5 sigma. Super-Eddington accretion models with a thermalising envelope reproduce the turnover, but only for a black hole ~2.5dex less massive than the dynamical estimate. For a dust-reddened accretion disc (A_V ~ 2 mag), dust at ~1200K can re-emit at most ~2 per cent of the absorbed luminosity, and most of it would have to emerge at ~70-600K, unless the dust covers only a small fraction of the sky. The dynamics favour an accretion-powered source, but our data cannot distinguish dust reddening from processing by dense gas. MIRI imaging at >18um could separate these scenarios.

entries.title: Validation of Habitable Zone Limits with a New Radiative-Convective Equilibrium Climate Model
entries.abstract: The habitable zone (HZ) boundaries calculated with the Clima one-dimensional radiative-convective equilibrium (RCE) model have served as a standard reference for exoplanet target selection for three decades, but they have never been independently validated with a comparable model. We present ExoColumn, a new one-dimensional RCE model that couples an independently developed atmospheric column physics package to the ExoRT correlated-k radiative transfer core that is also used by the three-dimensional ExoCAM model. We calibrate ExoColumn to present-day conditions, which matches other RCE models to within a few kelvin through the troposphere. Line-by-line benchmarks show that the ExoRT and Clima radiation cores each reproduce the outgoing longwave flux to within a few percent, with the differences due to the spectral line databases used by each model. We follow the same inverse climate modeling method as previous studies have done to find inner edge moist- and runaway-greenhouse limits of 0.970 au and 0.966 au, and an outer-edge maximum-greenhouse limit of 1.611 au at a CO$_2$ partial pressure of 8.7 bar. We extend these calculations to 12 host stars spanning 2000-7200 K and to planets of 0.1, 1, and 5 Earth mass, and we provide updated HZ boundary coefficients for community use. The ExoColumn limits systematically fall closer to the host star than those of Clima but agree to within a few percent in orbital distance, which validates the robustness of the published Clima HZ boundaries.

entries.title: Constraints on Cosmic-Rays and the MeV Emission from Jupiter's Atmosphere
entries.abstract: The Cosmic $γ$-ray Background (CGB) in the MeV regime remains among the least understood components of diffuse cosmic radiation, primarily due to instrumental limitations in detecting faint isotropic emission at MeV energies. We present an indirect method for probing isotropic emission from soft X-rays to $γ$-rays through scattered emission in Jupiter's atmosphere. Using archival observations from SPI, the spectrometer aboard INTEGRAL, spanning 22 years of serendipitous Jupiter observations, we analyse the planet as a moving $γ$-ray point source in the 30 keV to 8 MeV range. Our analysis focuses on Jupiter's $γ$-ray albedo, produced by high-energy photon and cosmic-ray interactions. We performed detailed Monte Carlo simulations to model the response of Jupiter's atmosphere to incident photons, protons, electrons, positrons, and alpha particles. We simulate a 1000 km deep spherical atmosphere with 1 km shell resolution, based on Galileo probe measurements. By comparing empirical and astrophysical models with the SPI data, we find no statistically significant emission from Jupiter. We derive $2σ$ upper limits across the 30 keV to 8 MeV band, which we compare with cutoff power-law, reflected CGB, cosmic-ray-induced, and long-lived mediator dark matter models. We constrain Jupiter's bremsstrahlung luminosity in the MeV range to $10^{18}$ erg/s, close to that inferred from in situ measurements obtained by Juno/JEDI. While the expected emission from the CGB and cosmic rays is a factor of $10^4$ and 100 below our upper limits, respectively, this work establishes planetary atmospheres as promising indirect probes of diffuse $γ$-ray backgrounds for future MeV missions.

entries.title: Violent relaxation redux
entries.abstract: Collisionless self-gravitating systems, such as merging galaxies, have long seemed an exception to the statistical-mechanical principle that chaotic many-body systems relax to maximum-entropy states: Lynden-Bell's statistical mechanics of their "violent relaxation," constrained by exact conservation of phase-space volume -- equivalently, of infinitely many collisionless "Casimir" invariants -- has appeared not to be a good description. We propose that violent relaxation does give rise to Lynden-Bell's maximum-entropy equilibria, but that both are underpinned by gravitational turbulence, in which large-scale gravitational fluctuations drive chaotic phase-space mixing of the particles' distribution function. We derive the universal small-scale (sub-Jeans) spectra of this turbulence and show that it leads to phase-space-volume conservation being broken on a timescale only logarithmically longer, in the particle number N, than the dynamical (violent-relaxation) time. This timescale separation lets the system relax "adiabatically" through a sequence of Lynden-Bell equilibria, each corresponding to instantaneous values of the Casimirs. At long times, it approaches an equilibrium close to its "ground state": a distribution whose Casimirs have adjusted so that the system's energy is now its minimum possible energy. Thus, the system's universal tendency is toward a minimum-energy, maximum-entropy state. We corroborate this picture with 1D N-body simulations and hypothesize that it can explain the universal equilibria of galaxies and dark-matter halos.

entries.title: Through Ups and Downs: the Transient Lensing Behaviour of SIDM halos undergoing Core Collapse
entries.abstract: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) haloes can become extremely dense following gravothermal core collapse, motivating their use as explanations for unusually concentrated gravitational lenses. Using an emulator calibrated on gravothermal fluid calculations, we investigate whether increasing central density necessarily strengthens lensing. We follow initially Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) haloes through core formation and collapse deep into the short-mean-free-path regime, and compute finite-source magnifications, critical curves, and source-plane lensing cross sections for isolated spherical haloes with elastic, velocity-independent self-interactions, including external shear in selected calculations. Lensing strength evolves non-monotonically: it initially decreases during core formation, rises during early collapse, and generally declines at later stages despite continued growth of the central density. This decline accompanies the emergence of a dense inner core whose mass and radius decrease within a more extended, lower-density core. Time-averaged enhancement relative to NFW haloes depends on the lensing statistic, halo concentration, and interaction cross section. Generalized NFW haloes with central cusps $ρ\propto r^{-γ}$ with $γ\geq 2$ always have larger lensing efficacies than core-collapsed SIDM haloes of equal mass and are therefore poor proxies, including in terms of the demographics (size and radial thickness) of arcs and Einstein rings. The core collapse stage at which SIDM haloes are optimal lenses coincides with the epoch at which the characteristic core surface density is close to critical, which typically occurs during the early stages of core collapse. These results demonstrate that central density alone is insufficient to characterize SIDM lensing and that its evolving mass distribution must be modelled explicitly.

entries.title: A joint astrometric, eclipse timing and radial velocity orbit for the hierarchical triple V819 Herculis
entries.abstract: We present a joint Bayesian orbital analysis of the hierarchical triple system V819 Herculis using ground-based astrometry, radial velocities (RV), and eclipse timing variations (ETV). By coupling these complementary data sets within a physically consistent Keplerian framework, we obtain a self-consistent three-dimensional solution for the outer orbit and the dynamical properties of the system. The outer orbit is found to have a period of $P_3 = 2016.97 \pm 0.27$ d and a high eccentricity of $e_3 = 0.6800 \pm 0.0016$, with the same orbital geometry simultaneously reproducing the sky-plane astrometry, the LiTE signal in the eclipse timings, and the tertiary radial velocities. The joint solution determines the component masses dynamically from these data alone, yielding $M_{12} = 2.721 \pm 0.055\,M_\odot$ for the inner binary and $M_3 = 1.954 \pm 0.070\,M_\odot$ for the tertiary, together with a LiTE amplitude of $A_\mathrm{LiTE} = 0.0104$ d and an RV semi-amplitude of $K_3 = 18.46$ km s$^{-1}$. The joint fit also yields an orbital parallax of $π_\mathrm{orb} = 14.08 \pm 0.13$ mas, consistent with Gaia DR3, Gaia DR2 and the HIPPARCOS New Reduction. The derived tertiary mass is higher than expected for a standard G8-type main-sequence star, suggesting that the tertiary component may be in an advanced evolutionary stage. The resulting outer orbit is well constrained, and the system is strongly hierarchical, with an outer period about 900 times the inner one.
